entries.title: I like SWTs
entries.html: A mathematical operation which yields the same coefficients despite translation, rotation and scaling of its inputs? There are these things called Scattering Wavelet Transforms, and they are pretty good at clustering unlabeled instrument samples taken from tracker modules. They might be good at comparing textures in images as well. Maybe biomedical applications? Who can really say...

entries.title: On the subconscious
entries.html: So, in the brain, structures that mimic the external world in their geometry arise. The conscious/subconscious dichotomy is nothing more than the brain imitating it's perception of reality: there is what we experience directly, i.e. that which we see, hear, touch, taste and smell, and then there is everything else that is happening elsewhere in the world. We aren't directly aware of it, but it does affect us, maybe not right this second, but certainly at some point in the future. So this external divide between what we are immediately aware of and everything else that is happening, is very cleverly mirrored in the way our minds work. There is the conscious process, which we are aware of and have direct control over, and then there is the subconscious process, which is like those events that we know take place but cannot experience directly. If there were a way to model this type of hidden process in a neural network, maybe via some type of one-way information flow during the training process, I would think that would be a major step on the path towards AGI.
